subject: Television & Streaming
title: Dick Wolf and the Franchise Model
description: A micro-lesson that makes Dick Wolf and the Franchise Model usable.

hook.text: Dick Wolf created Law & Order in 1990. Three decades later, his shows fill more hours of TV than any other producer.

buildup.text: Wolf perfected the procedural franchise—Law & Order, SVU, Chicago Fire, Chicago P.D.—each following the same formula.

discovery.text: His secret was efficiency. Every episode was self-contained, endlessly rerunnable, and cheap to syndicate.

twist.text: Critics dismissed his shows as factory-produced. Wolf didn't care—his franchises earned billions in syndication revenue.

climax.text: Wolf proved that television didn't need to be art to be successful. Reliable entertainment built an empire.

punchline.text: One formula, repeated a thousand times, built a TV empire.

quiz.question: What business model made Dick Wolf's TV empire so profitable?
options: Self-contained episodes that were easy to syndicate
